# RV power station and solar combos

The best combo depends on whether you need to run the roof A/C. The sources are mostly affiliate review sites, so check current prices before buying.

## Weekend or light use (fridge, lights, laptop, Starlink)
**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** is the top pick in one roundup. It has a 1,024Wh LiFePO4 battery, 1,800W output, and up to 1,000W of solar input (about 28 lb, expandable to 5kWh). Pair it with EcoFlow's folding panels. A single 200W panel works but charges slowly. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the simpler, lighter option. It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output, and weighs about 23.8 lb. Its solar input tops out at 400W, so two SolarSaga 200W panels is the most it can use. It isn't expandable. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

## Full-time RVing or running the A/C
A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so you need a bigger unit. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is that article's best all-rounder, with 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, and expansion past 12kWh. It is heavy, a two-person lift, and the most expensive option once you add batteries. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** has 3,024Wh and 3,000W, and is described as simpler to use. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **BLUETTI AC200L** is the mid-range value pick. It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W of solar input, and a built-in 30A RV port. It weighs about 62 lb. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **ALLPOWERS R4000** is a big-capacity value option with 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, an RV outlet, and 2,000W of solar input across three inputs. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb) and has a 5-year warranty. The store price was $1,499 on 10/23, and codes such as EXTRA10 or ALLPOWERS26 took 10% off in the store's cart. Codes expire in November and December, and checkout has the final word. ([Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh), [details](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Solar panels
- For a Jackery, use the SolarSaga 100W or 200W panels. ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html))
- A budget alternative is the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))
- Check the station's maximum solar input before sizing panels. A big array is wasted on a unit with a low ceiling, such as the Jackery's 400W. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))
- For a mid-size unit, 300–400W of folding panels can refill it in a full day of good sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## My pick
- **Most RVers without A/C:** EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with two or more folding panels.
- **A/C or full-time:** EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 for the most headroom, or the BLUETTI AC200L if you want something cheaper and lighter.

I couldn't open the retailers' pages here, so I can't give direct purchase links for the EcoFlow, Jackery, or BLUETTI models. The review pages above have price buttons for each. If you tell me your RV's A/C and fridge setup, and your budget, I can narrow it to one combo.
